title: VPC IaC CI: pre-apply drift scan, policy scoring, and Conftest catalog
creator: Aisha Chen
description:
Problem: Private (VPC) customer deployments require stronger pre-apply validation to avoid network/security regressions and unintentional resource drift. Current pipelines run a terraform plan and rely on human review, which is slow and inconsistent across repos. We need a standardized CI pattern to gate PRs for all private deployment IaC repositories that: 1) runs fast linting, 2) executes an isolated pre-apply drift scan against a read-only state snapshot, 3) scores changes against a shared OPA/Conftest policy catalog, and 4) produces a single actionable verdict + risk summary in the PR.

Goal: Build an opinionated, reusable CI template (GitHub Actions + optional Runner for air-gapped customers) and a central Conftest/OPA policy registry with semantic versions. The pipeline should be flexible so individual teams can opt-in emergency exemptions (audit + post-apply approval) but by default block high-risk changes (e.g., new public egress, open security groups, KMS key rotations without key policy review).

Scope and deliverables:
- A GitHub Actions workflow template (reusable workflow) that implements: terraform fmt/tflint/checkov quick scans, terraform init/plan using a read-only state snapshot, a drift-detection step comparing plan vs last-known state (drift scanner), Conftest/OPA policy evaluation with policy scoring, and an annotated PR comment summarizing findings.
- A Conftest policy registry (policies stored in a policies repo) with a documented release process and a compatibility matrix for Terraform module versions.
- A small 'policy-score' shim that converts Conftest results into a numeric risk score and maps to gating rules (e.g., score >= 7 -> block, 4-6 -> require 2nd approver, <4 -> informational).
- A plan-to-run mapping that allows pipelines in private offline deployments to run on a self-hosted runner with identical semantics.
- Acceptance criteria, test harness repos, and example migration PRs for 3 internal private repos: vpc-bootstrap, infra-networking, and redis-cluster.

Non-goals: Full automatic apply in CI, replacing infra owners' judgement, or rewriting existing Terraform modules as part of this ticket.

Implementation notes and trade-offs:
- Conftest (rego) chosen for initial parity with existing policies; we'll design policies to be exportable to OPA later. The policy registry will maintain rego snippets and a small set of test fixtures.
- Using a read-only state snapshot avoids making writes from CI. For private/on-prem, snapshots will be pulled from a secured artifact store (S3 or internal blob) or produced by a scheduled job.
- We will implement drift detection via diff of plan output vs last-applied resource attributes. This is best-effort and will be conservative (flag potential drift rather than attempt auto-fix).
- We prefer GitHub Actions reusable workflows for hosted customers and provide a runner-playbook for on-prem customers to ensure parity. Atlantis can be supported later but is out of scope here.

Acceptance criteria (high level):
- Reusable workflow added to infra-ci-templates that runs in <7 minutes for typical small PRs and provides deterministic exit codes for gating.
- Conftest policy registry with at least 12 policies covering network, IAM, storage, and KMS; policies have unit tests and changelog entries.
- Policy-score mapping documented and enforced by pipeline; at least one internal repo configured to block PR merge on high-risk score.
- Self-hosted-runner playbook and small container image published for private customers.
- Migration PRs created for vpc-bootstrap, infra-networking, redis-cluster showing green runs and documented exceptions.

Rollout plan:
1) Prototype pipeline in infra-ci-templates and land policy-registry skeleton (week 1).
2) Trial on vpc-bootstrap (week 2) to iterate on policy false positives.
3) Bind pipeline as required status check in two internal repos (week 3).
4) Publish runner playbook and documentation for private customers (week 4).

Monitoring and observability:
- CI runs should emit metrics to internal dashboard: avg run duration, policy violations per repo, false-positive rate (reported by teams).
- Create a webhook that forwards Conftest violations to a policy-triage Slack channel for initial tuning.

Backout and rollback:
- If the pipeline incorrectly blocks critical fixes, repo owners can temporarily bypass the gate via a documented emergency exemption flow that requires an audit ticket.

Documentation and training:
- Confluence doc: "Private IaC CI: pre-apply policy gating" (link below)
- Short walkthrough session for infra owners and customer success teams.

Links and references:
- Prototype workflow PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-ci-templates/pull/642
- Policy registry repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/policies
- Example migration PR (vpc-bootstrap): https://github.com/redwood-inference/vpc-bootstrap/pull/198
- Confluence design draft: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/123456789/Private+IaC+CI
- Related tickets: ENG-32812 (state-snapshot-service), ENG-32500 (runner-hardening)

Security considerations:
- Policy registry repo will be access-restricted; CI runner will fetch signed policy bundles. All signing keys managed via KMS.
- Ensure no secrets are echoed in PR comments; plan output scrubber will remove sensitive attributes before uploading artifacts.
acceptance_criteria: Reusable GitHub Actions workflow in infra-ci-templates with gating exit codes
Policy registry with 12+ Conftest policies and unit tests
Self-hosted runner playbook and container image for private deployments
Two internal private repos configured to fail PR merge on high-risk policy score
